The test image shows wheat leaves with elongated tan-to-brown lesions running along the leaf blade, with some darker brown centers and yellowing around them. The pattern is stripe-like and parallel to the leaf veins.

Key visual features:
- Large, elongated brown/tan blotches on leaves
- Darker brown necrotic centers within lesions
- Yellowish chlorotic halos around lesions
- Lesions oriented along leaf length

Top candidates: Tan Spot, Septoria Leaf Blotch, or Bacterial Leaf Streak. The elongated tan-brown lesions with darker centers are classic for Tan Spot. Let me view one reference image to confirm.

**Visual analysis summary:**
- Wheat leaves with large, elongated tan-to-brown lesions
- Lesions run along the leaf blade (parallel to veins)
- Dark brown necrotic centers within the lesions
- Yellowish chlorotic halos surrounding the lesions
- No visible orange/yellow pustules (ruling out rusts)
- No powder-like growth (ruling out Powdery Mildew)
- No distinct water-soaked streaks (less likely Bacterial Streak)

The elongated tan/brown lesions with darker brown centers and yellow halos are classic hallmarks of **Tan Spot** (*Pyrenophora tritici-repentis*). The shape, color gradient, and leaf-parallel orientation match this disease well. Septoria Leaf Blotch would show smaller, more irregular blotches with dark pycnidia specks; Bacterial Leaf Streak would show more linear, water-soaked pale streaks.
